title: Activation and commands
summary: Laravel records what should run (desired state); the Go runtime decides what does run (applied state) and reports back. Intent travels as rows in Laravel's device_outbox, which the runtime claims over internal HTTP and applies one at a time. Every message carries the device's generation, so late or repeated work is dropped on both sides.

boxes.label: Device services
boxes.detail: Activation, deactivation and command confirmation each run in one database transaction under a lock on the device row. They change the desired state, raise deployment_generation by one for a configuration change, and write the outbox row in the same commit. Laravel never calls the runtime to apply anything.

boxes.label: device_outbox
boxes.detail: One row per message: device.activate.v1, device.deactivate.v1, device.command.v1 and the workflow deployments. A row is claimed with a lease token for 30 seconds, up to 100 rows a call, and is marked published only by an acknowledgement that carries the current token. An expired lease puts the row back in the next claim.

boxes.label: Runtime relay
boxes.detail: One loop in the runtime. It POSTs outbox/claim with a bearer token, publishes each row to JetStream with the row's UUID as the message ID, then acknowledges the row. A publish that fails stops the batch and leaves the rest for the next claim. The same loop publishes the runtime's own outbox in the other direction.

boxes.label: IOT_DEVICE_CONTROL
boxes.detail: A file-backed JetStream stream that keeps messages for seven days and refuses new ones when it is full, so work then waits in device_outbox. The message ID makes a row published twice appear once.

boxes.label: device_runtime
boxes.detail: The runtime's own schema. device_runtime.devices holds each device's generation, applied definition, applied_generation and last outcome. A change there and its event row in device_runtime.outbox commit together, so the runtime never applies something it cannot report.

boxes.label: IOT_DEVICE_EVENTS
boxes.detail: Runtime events on their way to Laravel: device.applied.v1, device.failed.v1, device.deactivated.v1, command.status.v1 and the presence, discovery and automation events.

boxes.label: Event inbox
boxes.detail: Takes up to 200 unacknowledged events from the stream and posts them in stream order, at most 100 events or 1 MiB a batch. A batch Laravel cannot take yet is retried in place, so no later event overtakes it. An event Laravel will never accept is dead-lettered on its own.

boxes.label: Event receiver
boxes.detail: Applies a batch in one transaction, each event in its own savepoint. The event UUID goes into device_inbox first, so a repeat is answered as a duplicate. An outcome is applied only when its generation, operation and configuration match the device's pending operation; anything else is answered as stale and changes nothing.

steps.text: A person activates a configuration. Laravel points the device's desired pointer at a new snapshot, marks the deployment pending and raises the generation by one.
The same transaction writes a device.activate.v1 row. If the commit fails there is no message; if it succeeds the message cannot be lost.
The runtime asks for work every second. Laravel leases it up to 100 rows for 30 seconds each.
Each row is published to JetStream and then acknowledged with its lease token. A row whose lease ran out is claimed again; the message ID stops it appearing twice.
The control consumer handles one message at a time. A failure is retried with a growing delay; a message that can never be read is dead-lettered.
It applies the configuration only if the generation is newer than the last one it handled, and writes the new state and a device.applied.v1 or device.failed.v1 event in one transaction.
The relay publishes the event from the runtime's outbox to the events stream.
The inbox posts events to Laravel in ordered batches and retries a batch in place until Laravel takes it.
Laravel moves the applied pointer only when the event matches the device's current generation and pending operation. An older event is answered as stale.
A confirmed command takes the same road as device.command.v1 and is dispatched once, as an NCMD or DCMD.
Each command outcome is stored with a command.status.v1 event and travels back the same way.
Open the control consumer to follow one activation step by step, including the wait for a birth and a stale generation.
